evidence.note: The exothermic decomposition in synthesis gas from 200 °C is cited from Kawamura and Irie.; quote withheld: sha256:c65a744f9d0b849048dfa037da3d60c3bf91590e38ae457e916dd2e6c724e7eb chars:245

props.note: The 200 °C exothermic decomposition in synthesis gas is cited, not measured here.
props.statement: The hydroxychromate of A0-3 decomposes in air endothermically at about 310 °C, a different type from the decomposition in synthesis gas (exothermic, from about 200 °C according to Kawamura and Irie); the endothermic peak is due to the conversion of sexivalent chromium oxide by oxygen removal into the trivalent oxide, which combines with zinc oxide to form zinc chromite.

props.name: air heating lowers k'; main reason B is less active
props.statement: k' depends on Cr/Zn nearly as k does. In series A both high k' and moderately large S give the high k; in series B k' is the sole factor, S being nearly equal for all. Heating the chromium-containing catalysts in air at 400 °C lowers k' considerably, and since the air-heated catalysts have larger surface areas after synthesis, this decrease in k' is the main reason why series B is less active.

props.name: by-products at 380 °C
props.statement: In the liquid products at 380 °C, dimethyl ether (0.7-1.5%), methyl formate (0.5-0.6%) and formaldehyde (0.1%) are nearly independent of catalyst or chromium content; water is said to be higher with lower-activity catalysts (5% for A-3, 1.1% for A-1, as printed); isobutanol was never detectable.

props.name: zinc chromite lattice larger than normal; ZnO normal
props.note: The literature values are cited (A.S.T.M. data file).
props.statement: The zinc oxide lattice constants vary little and agree with the literature value (3.249 Å); the zinc chromite lattice constants of the catalysts (8.397-8.523 Å) are generally greater than the literature values (8.32, 8.20 Å) and stay enlarged after prolonged heating in hydrogen at 500 °C.

props.name: the two series differ structurally under the electron microscope
props.statement: Reduction of A0-3 produces caterpillar-like particles about 50 Å wide (aggregates of ca. 50 Å crystallites) within the fringe of the hydroxychromate crystal, which grow with gaps during synthesis (probably sintering); the air-heated B0-3 resembles A0-3 and B1-3 stays mostly homogeneous; heating in hydrogen at 500 °C causes marked crystal growth, more in B1-3.

props.name: hydroxychromates decompose to ZnO and zinc chromite
props.statement: Original A0-2 contains hydroxychromate IIIβ with zinc oxide, A0-3 hydroxychromate Iβ alone, and the highest-chromium catalyst an unidentified pattern; after reduction in synthesis gas or use in synthesis only zinc oxide and zinc chromite are seen, so the hydroxychromates have decomposed; heating in air at 400 °C also decomposes them (B0), B0-4 showing unidentified intermediates.

props.name: optimum Cr/Zn 0.5; unheated series A more active than air-heated B
props.statement: The optimum chromium/zinc atomic ratio is 0.5 in each series, and every catalyst of series A (not heated in air) is more active than the corresponding catalyst of series B (heated in air at 400 °C, 5 h), although series A has much smaller surface areas after synthesis (k330: A-3 17.9×10^-2, B-3 15.2×10^-2 atm^-2.1 hr^-1).

props.name: BET-derived particle size disagrees with electron microscopy
props.statement: The average particle diameter d = 6/ρtS differs greatly from the sizes seen by electron microscopy (e.g. A0-3: about 4000 Å cube vs. thin plates of several thousand Å; A2-3: 160 Å vs. caterpillars about 50 Å wide); the discrepancies of A0-3 and A2-3 are explained by particle shape, that of B1-3 cannot be explained satisfactorily, and d is of minor significance.

props.name: used-catalyst particles are aggregates of ZnO and chromite crystallites
props.statement: After removal of free zinc oxide the residue of A2-3 has Cr/Zn 1.79 (about that of zinc chromite) and looks essentially like the initial sample, so most particles of A2-3 are aggregates of zinc oxide and zinc chromite crystallites, the others zinc oxide alone or mainly; in B1-3 the residue shows wide openings, so the two components are locally concentrated and their mutual penetration is less thorough than in A2-3.

props.name: series A more thermally stable
props.statement: Comparing A-3 with A'-3 and B-3 with B'-3 (after 8 h in hydrogen at 500 °C) gives an approximate concept of relative thermal stability; series A is the more thermally stable. Heating for only 2 h in hydrogen lowered activity as much as 8 h.

props.name: surface area depends on treatment history
props.statement: Original chromium-containing catalysts (A0) have very small surface areas, smaller than the zinc oxide catalyst; reduction in synthesis gas enlarges them 30-50 times; use in synthesis then lowers them, the more the lower the chromium content. Air heating at 400 °C slightly increases them; after synthesis the air-heated catalysts (B1) have larger areas than A2, nearly the same for all chromium contents. Heating in hydrogen at 500 °C for 8 h after synthesis markedly decreases the area, more for B1-3. Helium density decreases with chromium content; particles of the original catalysts are large and split into very fine particles on reduction.

props.name: reactants reach a coherent surface smaller than the particle surface
props.statement: The surface of all particles estimated from micrographs can exceed the BET area; following Nielsen, interfacial layers coalesce into a coherent surface, and this coherent surface, which the reactants reach, should be used in interpreting k through specific activity and surface area.

props.name: slow decomposition in synthesis gas vs. sudden decomposition in air
props.statement: The structural difference between the series may stem from how zinc hydroxychromate decomposes: in synthesis gas slowly but more completely (excess oxygen removed as CO2), fine ZnO and zinc chromite crystallites forming at low temperature and serving as nuclei for large particles in which the two interpenetrate thoroughly; in air suddenly at 310 °C, into very fine crystallites scattered in the fringe of the layer structure with incomplete oxygen removal, a structure hard to transform later in synthesis gas.

props.name: specific activity follows ZnO-chromite interpenetration, not lattice constant
props.statement: The specific activity cannot be correlated with the zinc chromite lattice constant (which varies little while k' differs greatly between series); the difference in specific activity is attributed to the degree of mutual penetration of zinc oxide and zinc chromite, consistent with the rise of B'-3's specific activity to the level of A-3 after heating in hydrogen at 500 °C, which favours that penetration.

props.name: excess Zn2+ in interstices of non-stoichiometric chromite enlarges its lattice
props.statement: Taking Irie and Shiraishi's view (low-temperature chromite occludes zinc oxide), where the zinc chromite is non-stoichiometric, Zn2+ enters the empty interstices, enlarging and stressing the lattice. The broadening of the chromite lines after removal of the excess zinc oxide is probably due to the stress this removal imposes.
